{{About|the block|the mob|Creaking}} {{Infobox block | group = Uprooted | group2 = Dormant | group3 = Active | 1-1 = Creaking Heart.png | 2-1 = Dormant Creaking Heart JE1 BE1.png | 3-1 = Active Creaking Heart.png | invimage = | rarity = common | renewable = Yes | light = No | transparent = No | flammable = No | lavasusceptible = No | stackable = Yes (64) | tool = axe }} A '''creaking heart''' is a 'living' [[block]]{{Citation|author=Sophie Austin |title=The Pale Garden |url=https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/the-pale-garden |website=minecraft.net |date=2 October 2024 |quote=While creaking hearts might look like wood, these are actually living blocks}}{{snap|24w40a|October 2, 2024}} that can be [[crafted]] or found in [[pale oak]] trees in [[pale garden]]s. It activates if placed in a line between two [[pale oak log]]s; then, during [[Daylight cycle|nighttime]], it spawns a [[creaking]] and protects it from all [[damage]]. [[Breaking]] a creaking heart that is protecting a creaking instantly kills it. Hitting a protected creaking causes [[resin clump]]s to grow on [[pale oak log]]s near its linked creaking heart. == Obtaining == === Breaking === Creaking hearts drop as an item only when mined by a tool enchanted with [[Silk Touch]]. Otherwise, they drop 1–3 [[resin clump]]s; [[Fortune]] can increase the maximum drops by 1 per level (up to 6 with Fortune III). Destroying a naturally-generated creaking heart also drops 20–24 [[experience]], only in [[Survival]] mode. Creaking heart has the highest [[hardness]] value of all blocks having the axe as the suitable tool. {{Breaking row|horizontal=1|Creaking Heart|link=none|Axe|drop=0}} === Natural generation === Creaking hearts have a 10% chance to generate inside the top trunks of [[pale oak]] trees in the [[pale garden]]. They are always completely covered by other [[pale oak log]]s and are never exposed to the air. Pale oaks grown from [[pale oak sapling]]s do not generate with hearts. Creaking hearts can also generate in certain [[abandoned camp]] variants. {{Block distribution}} === Crafting === {{Crafting |B1=Pale Oak Log |B2=Block of Resin |B3=Pale Oak Log |Output=Creaking Heart |type=Decoration block}} == Usage == A creaking heart can be placed in different orientations, similar to [[log]]s. It has three states: uprooted, dormant, and awake. The creaking heart is uprooted by default, but it becomes dormant during the day and awake at night when placed between two [[pale oak log]]s, [[stripped pale oak log]]s, [[pale oak wood]], or [[stripped pale oak wood]] with the same orientation. The texture of a creaking heart changes depending on its state, with the "core" appearing dark when uprooted, brighter when dormant and orange when awake. If the creaking heart hasn't already spawned a [[creaking]], removing one of the surrounding aligned logs reverts it to the uprooted state. Creaking hearts generate [[resin clump]]s on nearby pale oak logs when its linked creaking is attacked by a [[player]] or tamed [[wolf]] at night. There is a 5-second cooldown between each resin clump generation. === Spawning mechanics === {{Main|Creaking#Spawning}} [[File:Creaking Heart In Java Edition.png|right|thumb|A disabled creaking heart (left) and an active creaking heart (right)]] If a creaking heart is properly aligned between two pale oak logs and is located in the [[Overworld]], it becomes awake at [[night]] (between 12600 and 23400 ticks). An awake creaking heart waits 2 [[tick]]s (0.1 seconds) and checks if the matching logs are in place. If so and it detects no linked creaking, it tries to find a valid location in a 33×17×33 box centered at that creaking heart to spawn one until successful, interrupted by getting destroyed or disabled. If found, it waits 20 ticks (1 second) before checking again if the matching logs are in place. If successful, it spawns a creaking after 2 extra ticks, otherwise it uproots. While a creaking heart is awake and has a linked creaking, it does not uproot until broken, even if any of the matching blocks are removed. [[File:Creaking Heart Spawning Box.png|alt=The 33×17×33 box in which a Creaking Heart is able to spawn its Creaking.|thumb|Creaking can spawn in yellow or brown regions when provided with a valid spawning space by a spawnable block placed in yellow or orange regions and three blocks of air above it.]] Valid locations for creakings to spawn at follow these criteria: * The block below must have a solid top surface. * The block below is not [[leaves]]. * The location is any non-solid block. This means blocks like [[carpet]] can spawn-proof creakings, but not [[button]]s. * The location is where there would be no [[liquid]] or other entities' [[hitbox]]es within a creaking's hitbox. ** Due to a bug {{note|{{bug|MCPE-189513}}}}, creakings can be spawned in water {{in|Bedrock}}. [[Creaking]]s ignore solid blocks within its hitbox that are 2+ blocks above the ground while spawning. Creaking hearts never spawn creakings in [[the Nether]] nor [[the End]]. === Despawning creakings === Breaking the heart kills its linked creaking and attributes the kill to the [[player]] who broke it, adding the kill to their [[statistics]] and triggering the Monster Hunter and Monsters Hunted [[advancement]]s. During daytime (starting at 23401 ticks), an awake creaking heart becomes dormant and despawns its linked creakings, unless it has been named using a [[name tag]]. If the heart's linked creaking is too far away (more than 34 blocks away), that creaking despawns, and the heart spawns another one if conditions are met. A creaking heart cannot be disabled by removing the log above or below it during the night.{{bug|MC-277171||Creaking Heart does not disable when log is removed from above or below during night|Works as Intended}} === Redstone component === A [[redstone comparator]] connected to a creaking heart outputs a signal if the heart has a linked creaking. The strength of the signal depends on the [[Euclidean distance]] between the heart and its creaking, and is calculated as follows: \text{output} = 15 - \left\lfloor \frac{\text{distance}}{32} \times15 \right\rfloor In other words, the closer a creaking is to its heart, the stronger the signal. Additionally, a creaking itself can be used to detect when a [[player]] is looking at it. An observed creaking sinks in [[water]] (or [[lava]]) instead of swimming upward, which can cause it to activate a [[pressure plate]] or similar means. An unobserved creaking bobs up and down in liquid, which can cause it to activate a pressure plate even if not being looked at. Giving a creaking enough space to bob prevents this. [[Piston]]s of any kind cannot move creaking hearts. === Ambient sounds === A creaking heart emits subtle [[#Unique|eerie sounds]] when it is awake and surrounded by any types of [[log]]s, [[stripped log]]s, [[wood]], or [[stripped wood]] in all 6 directions. == Sounds == === Generic === {{Sound table/Block/Creaking heart}} === Unique === {{Edition|Java}}: {{SoundTable |type=java |{{SoundLine |sound=Creaking heart trail1.ogg |sound2=Creaking heart trail2.ogg |sound3=Creaking heart trail3.ogg |sound4=Creaking heart trail4.ogg |sound5=Creaking heart trail5.ogg |sound6=Creaking heart trail6.ogg |sound7=Creaking heart trail7.ogg |subtitle=Creaking Heart grumbles |source=block |description=When a creaking heart's creaking is attacked by a player |id=block.creaking_heart.hurt |translationkey=subtitles.block.creaking_heart.hurt |volume=''Varies''Plays ten times with an interval of 10 ticks starting at 1 and linearly interpolating to 0.55. It functions almost identically to a normal wooden chest, except that it [[oxidize]]s over time, and [[copper golem]]s remove items from it to store inside nearby wooden chests. Like normal chests, two copper chests can merge into a '''large copper chest''' if placed adjacent each other. == Obtaining == === Breaking === A copper chest drops itself only if mined with a [[stone pickaxe]] or better. Using any other item to mine a copper chest drops only its contents. {{breaking row|horizontal=1|Copper Chest|Pickaxe|Stone}} === Crafting === {{Crafting |head=1 |A1=Copper Ingot |A2=Copper Ingot |A3=Copper Ingot |B1=Copper Ingot |B2=Chest |B3=Copper Ingot |C1=Copper Ingot |C2=Copper Ingot |C3=Copper Ingot |Output=Copper Chest |type=Decoration block }} {{Crafting |Matching Unwaxed Copper Chest |Honeycomb |Output=Matching Waxed Copper Chest |type=Decoration block |foot=1 }} === Natural generation === Oxidized copper chests can generate as part of [[abandoned camp]]s. === Post-generation === {{main|Copper Golem#Spawning}} Upon creating a [[copper golem]] by placing a [[carved pumpkin]] or [[jack o'lantern]] next to a [[block of copper]], a copper chest is generated at the location of the copper block. Both the chest and the golem are spawned with their [[oxidation]] state matching that of the block of copper, but do not generate [[waxing|waxed]] even when a waxed block of copper is used. == Usage == [[File:Copper golem searches copper chest.png|thumb|A copper golem opens a copper chest to search for items to pick up.]] A copper chest placed adjacent to another copper chest joins to create a large copper chest. Two adjacent copper chests merge into a large copper chest even if the two chests have different oxidization levels or waxed states; in such cases, the resulting large chest takes the oxidization level of the least oxidized half, and is unwaxed if one of the two halves is unwaxed.{{bug|MC-300050||Placing different copper chests next to each other combines them into a large copper chest|WAI}} A player can prevent the formation of a large chest, and place two small copper chests side by side, by {{control|sneaking|sneak}} while placing the second chest {{in|java}}, pushing a copper chest into place with a [[piston]] {{in|bedrock}}, or placing the second chest facing a different direction from the first chest. {{IN|java}}, copper chests cannot be moved by [[piston]]s, and [[sticky pistons]]. === Copper golem === {{main|Copper Golem#Chest interactions and item transportation}} If a copper golem is not holding an item, it visits up to 10 copper chests (regardless of their oxidization or waxed status) in sequence to try to take out up to 16 of the first item contained within. The search area for copper chests from the copper golem's position is 32 blocks horizontally and 8 blocks vertically.{{Info needed|Is it taxicab or euclidian?}} === Container === A copper chest can be used as a container and has 27 slots of inventory space, and a large copper chest has twice that amount, at 54 slots. In the ''Java Edition'' interface, the top three rows for a large copper chest correspond to the left half of the copper chest when facing it, and the bottom three rows correspond to the right half. In ''Bedrock Edition'', the top three rows correspond to whichever half was placed first and the bottom three to the other half. Copper chests open when {{ctrl|used}}. To move items between the copper chest inventory and the player inventory or hotbar while the copper chest GUI is open, drag or shift-click the items. {{IN|java}}, holding {{key|Shift}} and double-clicking while holding an item moves all items of the type clicked on in or out of the copper chest, to the extent that space is available for them. To exit the copper chest GUI, use the {{key|Escape}} control. A copper chest cannot be opened if there is a [[conductive]] block above it ({{in|bedrock|lc=}}, bottom slabs prevent copper chests from being opened). Solid faces do not prevent copper chests from opening, so the lid of the copper chest can phase through blocks such as bottom-half [[slab]]s{{only|JE}}, [[stairs]], and [[non-conductive]] full cubes such as [[glass]] and [[ice]]. [[Cat]]s sitting on copper chests prevent them from opening. Because copper chests themselves are non-conductive, two copper chests can be stacked on top of one another while still allowing the lower copper chest to be opened. Players can open copper chests when they are being hurt ([[effect]] of Instant Damage, Poison, Wither, on fire, damaged by other [[player]]s or [[mob]]s, etc.). By default, the GUI of a copper chest is labeled "Copper Chest"{{only|be|short=1}}/"Chest"{{only|je|short=1}} and the GUI of a large copper chest is labeled "Large Copper Chest"{{only|be|short=1}}/"Large Chest".{{only|je|short=1}} A copper chest's GUI label can be changed by naming the chest in an [[anvil]] before placing it, or, {{in|java}}, by using the {{cmd|data}} command (for example, to label a chest at (0,64,0) as "Bonus Chest!", use {{cmd|data merge block 0 64 0 {CustomName:'"Bonus Chest!"'}}}). If half of a large copper chest is renamed, that name is used to label the GUI of the entire large copper chest, but if the named half is destroyed the other half reverts to the default label. If both halves of a large copper chest have different names, the GUI uses the name of the northernmost or westernmost half. {{IN|java}}, a copper chest can be "locked" by setting its {{nbt|compound|lock}} tag using the {{cmd|data}} command. If a chest's {{nbt|compound|lock}} tag is not blank, the copper chest cannot be opened unless the player is holding an item with the same name as the lock tag's text. For example, to lock a copper chest at (0,64,0) so that the copper chest cannot be opened unless the player is holding an item named "Copper Chest Key", use {{cmd|data merge block 0 64 0 {lock:{components:{"custom_name":"Copper Chest Key"}}}}}. === Oxidation === {{main|Oxidation}} Non-waxed copper chests have four stages of oxidation (including the initial normal state). [[Lightning bolt]]s, and using an [[axe]] while sneaking can remove the oxidation on copper chests. Using a [[honeycomb]] on a copper chest prevents it from oxidizing. As the block begins to oxidize (exposed), it gets discolored and green spots begin to appear. As the oxidation continues (weathered), the block is a green color with brown spots. In the last stage (oxidized), the block is teal with several green spots. === Piglins === [[Piglin]]s become hostile toward players who open or break a copper chest. == Sounds == === Generic === This process takes 8.62 seconds on average. During the transformation, any items held by the copper golem are [[drops|dropped]]. == Usage == === Posing === {{control|Interacting}} with a copper golem statue changes its pose, cycling through four poses: standing, sitting, running, and star. {{IN|bedrock}}, the player's hand must be empty in order to cycle through poses. Copper torches can also be used to craft [[copper lantern]]s. == Obtaining == === Breaking === Copper torches can be [[instant mining|broken instantly]] using anything, and drop themselves as an item. {{breaking row|Copper Torch|horizontal=1}} A copper torch is removed and drops itself as an item if: *Its attachment block is moved, removed, or destroyed *[[Water]] flows into its space *A [[piston]] pushes it or moves a block into its space When [[lava]] flows into a copper torch's space, it will be destroyed without dropping anything. === Crafting === {{Crafting |B1= Copper Nugget |B2= Coal; Charcoal |B3= Stick |Output= Copper Torch, 4 |type= Decoration block |foot=1}} == Usage == Copper torches can be placed on the top or the sides of most solid blocks, although some blocks require {{control|sneaking}}. Being non-solid, copper torches have no collision box. More information about placement can be found at [[Opacity/Placement]]. Gravity-affected blocks like [[sand]] and [[gravel]] do not start falling if the space immediately beneath is occupied by a copper torch. [[Falling Block|Falling blocks]] break if they fall onto a solid block with a copper torch above it. If there is an [[air]] block under the copper torch, the falling blocks fall through the copper torch onto the surface below.{{bug|MC-3262|||WAI}} Copper torches do not [[oxidize]]. The copper is being used as part of the torch's fuel and not the base. === Light === Copper torches give off a light level of 14. Copper torches also melt [[snow layer]]s within 2 blocks and [[ice]] within 3 blocks ([[taxicab distance]]). When the [[Render Dragon Features for Creators]] experiment is enabled in ''[[Minecraft Preview]]'', the top part of copper torches emits colored [[Vibrant Visuals#Point lighting|point lighting]] with {{Color|#86ca59}}. A '''copper chain''' is an oxidizing directional [[block]] and the [[copper]] variant of [[chain]]s.

== Obtaining ==
=== Breaking ===
Copper chains can be mined using any [[pickaxe]]. If mined without a pickaxe, they drop nothing.

== Usage ==
{{for|information about the placement mechanics of all chains|Chain#Usage}}
Copper chains share much of their functionality with their iron counterparts.

=== Oxidation ===
{{main|Oxidation}}
Non-waxed copper chains have four stages of oxidation (including the initial normal state). [[Lightning bolt]]s and [[axe]]s can remove the oxidation on copper chains. They can be waxed with [[honeycomb]] to prevent oxidation from progressing.

As the block begins to oxidize (exposed), it gets discolored and green spots begin to appear. As the oxidation continues (weathered), the block is a green color with brown spots. In the last stage (oxidized), the block is teal with several green spots.

'''Copper bars''' are [[copper]] variants of [[bars]]. Unlike [[iron bars]], they are colored copper orange and can [[oxidize]] over time, similar to other copper blocks.

== Obtaining ==

Copper bars can be mined using any [[pickaxe]]. If mined without a pickaxe, nothing is dropped.

== Usage ==
{{for|information about the placement mechanics of all bars|Bars#Usage}}

=== Oxidation ===
{{main|Oxidation}}
Non-waxed copper bars have four stages of oxidation (including the initial normal state). [[Lightning bolt]]s and [[axe]]s can remove the oxidation on copper bars. They can be waxed with [[honeycomb]] to prevent oxidation from progressing.

As the block begins to oxidize (exposed), it gets discolored and green spots begin to appear. As the oxidation continues (weathered), the block is a green color with brown spots. In the last stage (oxidized), the block is teal with several green spots.

A '''copper lantern''' is a [[copper]] variant of a [[lantern]] that displays a green flame and oxidizes over time.

== Obtaining ==
=== Breaking ===
A copper lantern can be mined with anything, but [[pickaxe]]s are the fastest. A copper lantern also breaks and drops itself if a [[piston]] extends or pushes a block into its location, or if its supporting block is moved or destroyed.

=== Natural generation ===
An oxidized copper lantern is generated in [[abandoned camp]]s.

== Usage ==
{{Main|Opacity/Placement}}Similarly to other types of lanterns, copper lanterns can either be placed on top of, or hung from, the surfaces of most solid blocks (though some blocks will require sneaking).

To place a copper lantern on top of a block, aim at the block's top face, and press use. To hang a copper lantern from the bottom of a block, aim at the block's bottom face, and press use. Also similarly to other lanterns, if a copper lantern is hung from the bottom face of a chain, the lantern and the chain will connect seamlessly.

Soul lanterns can also be placed by pressing use on a block adjacent to an air block the copper lantern could occupy, much like other types of lantern. Pressing use on the top half of the adjacent block will hang the lantern from the bottom of an above block, and pressing use on the bottom half of the adjacent block will place the lantern down on the top face of a bottom block.

Like other types of lantern, if a copper lantern exists on an invalid surface (a surface where the copper lantern could not normally be placed on), the copper lantern will break and drop itself, upon the invalid surface receiving a block update.

=== Light ===
The copper lantern is among the [[Light#Light-emitting blocks|most luminous of light sources]], emitting a light level of 15. Copper lanterns also melt [[Snow layer|snow layers]] within 2 blocks and [[ice]] within 3 blocks ([[taxicab distance]]).

When the [[Render Dragon Features for Creators]] experiment is enabled in ''[[Minecraft Preview]]'', the inside of all copper lanterns emits colored [[Vibrant Visuals#Point lighting|point lighting]] with {{Color|#86ca59}} for the unaffected unwaxed variant, and {{Color|#e8c398}} for all other variants. The casing of the copper lantern blocks a part of the light and casts some shadows around the lantern.

=== Oxidation ===
{{main|Oxidation}}
Non-waxed copper lanterns have four stages of oxidation (including the initial normal state). [[Lightning bolt]]s and [[axe]]s can remove the oxidation on copper lanterns. Using a [[honeycomb]] on a copper lantern prevents it from oxidizing.

As the block begins to oxidize (exposed), it gets discolored and green spots begin to appear. As the oxidation continues (weathered), the block is a green color with brown spots. In the last stage (oxidized), the block is teal with several green spots.

Unlike [[copper bulb]]s, the light level of a copper lantern is unaffected by its oxidation stage; even an oxidized copper lantern will still emit a light level of 15.
